channel.title: Thomas Lavigne
channel.description: Thomas Lavigne, PhD in biomechanics (biomécanique), specialized in vascular mechanics, poromechanics, hydrogels, and numerical simulation (fenics and fenicsx). Personal research webpage presenting projects in FEniCSx, Gmsh, porous media modeling, publications, CV, and post-doctoral work at ENS Paris-Saclay, I2M Bordeaux, Université du Luxembourg, LMS Polytechnique, and the IBHGC laboratory at ENSAM Paris.

item.title: Honored to receive the Excellent Thesis Award at the 2025 University of Luxembourg PhD Graduation.
item.description:
On December 10, 2025, I reached a major milestone at the University of Luxembourg’s PhD Graduation ceremony, where I officially received my doctoral diploma.

I am incredibly honored to announce that I was also the recipient of an Excellent Thesis Award (ETA) from the University of Luxembourg. It was a privilege to be called on stage to accept this prize and celebrate alongside friends and colleagues in the presence of the Rector, Vice-Rector, and the Minister of Higher Education. I was also grateful for the opportunity to present a portion of my research to the audience.

None of this would have been possible without the support of many incredible people. A heartfelt thank you to: - My Funding: The FNR (Grant AFR-FNR 17013812) for believing in this project. - My Mentors: My supervisors for their guidance. - My Network: My colleagues, friends, and family for their unwavering support. - The Unsung Heroes: The admin support, IT teams, HR, and doctoral schools who work behind the scenes to make projects like this come to life. - The Volunteers: Thank you for making the ceremony such a memorable event.

You can watch the recording of the ceremony here: (https://www.youtube.com/live/2Aq1HwV_Lv8)

As part of a cotutelle program, I look forward to receiving my second diploma from ENSAM later this year.

item.title: FEniCSx install for MCIA HPC
item.description:
As part of my post-doc at I2M, I had the opportunity to install FEniCSx 0.9.0 now available as a module on MCIA Curta cluster for all users.

Installation Update

After successful compilation and testing on the Curta cluster, the 0.9.0 stable release of the FEniCSx project is now accessible to all researchers and students using the MCIA resources. This installation ensures that users can leverage the most recent improvements in finite element solving without managing complex local environments or containers.

This module includes the full FEniCSx stack:

  • DOLFINx: The computational environment.
  • Basix: Finite element definitions.
  • UFL: Unified Form Language.
  • FFCx: Form Compiler.

This module also includes other scientific libraries like Neper, nlopt, skopt, …

How to use it

To use the new installation, you simply need to load the module in your SLURM scripts or interactive sessions. As per MCIA standards, the environment is managed via module.

1. Check availability:

module avail fenicsx

2. Load the module: You can load the specific version (recommended for reproducibility) or the default alias:

# Load specific version (0.9.0)
module load fenicsx/0.9.0

# OR load default
module load fenicsx

3. Verify the installation: Once loaded, you can verify the version directly in Python:

python3 -c "import dolfinx; print(f'DOLFINx version: {dolfinx.__version__} installed at {dolfinx.__path__[0]}')"

Big thanks to the MCIA support team for their assistance with the dependencies on the cluster. Happy coding!

For more details please give a look to these tutorials

item.title: PhD Defense
item.description:
I successfully defended my PhD as part of a cotutelle program between Université du Luxembourg & Arts et Métiers ParisTech - École Nationale Supérieure d’Arts et Métiers (i-biomec I2M – Institut de Mécanique et d’Ingénierie de Bordeaux)

My thesis, entitled “Biomechanical Response of Human Skin: a Hierarchical Porous Media Framework”, explored and evaluated a novel two-compartment porous model to capture the interaction between the mechanical behavior of soft tissues and microcirculatory response.

This journey was made possible thanks to the support and mentorship of my supervisors: Stéphane P.A. Bordas (FLSW), Pierre-Yves Rohan and Giuseppe Sciumè.

I’m also grateful to the jury and expert members for the rich and insightful discussions during the defence: Yohan Payan, Stéphane Avril, Christian Vincenot, Dr.-Ing. Silvia Budday, and Sébastien LAPORTE.

A special thank you as well to our collaborating laboratories -Laboratoire de Biologie Tissulaire et Ingénierie thérapeutique (LBTI), Institut FEMTO-ST, Laboratoire de Mécanique Paris-Saclay)- whose contributions, especially on the experimental side, were essential.

Heartfelt thanks to the volunteers who participated in the experimental cohorts and to all the individuals who contributed to this PhD.

Finally, I am honoured to have been proposed for the Pierre Béziers prize (ENSAM), Excellent Thesis Award (University of Luxembourg), the FNR Outstanding PhD Thesis, and the pre-selection for Prix Tarrach of Les Amis du Luxembourg.

This work was supported by the Luxembourg National Research Fund (FNR) under grant n° 17013182.

On to the next chapter!

#Biomechanics #PorousMedia #SoftTissues #Microcirculation #CotutellePhD

item.title: Visiting Brainiacs laboratory at FAU
item.description:
Thanks to collaborations with Pr. S. Budday, we had the distinct opportunity to spend a productive week visiting the new, state-of-the-art laboratory of the brainiacs research team at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (FAU). This highly collaborative visit allowed us to be warmly received by the group and gain in-depth exposure to their advanced work in brain experimentation and computational modeling. The trip served to strengthen research ties and provided invaluable insights into cutting-edge methodologies for both the physical study and the numerical simulation of complex brain mechanics.

We’re excited about the possibility of reconducting this initiative in the future!
